title: Digital Input and Output with Arduino
learning_objectives: Configure a pin as digital input or output using pinMode()
Turn an LED on and off using digitalWrite()
Read a button state using digitalRead()
Use INPUT_PULLUP to simplify button wiring
Write a program that responds to input in real time
introduction: Digital pins are the simplest form of communication between a microcontroller and the outside world. A digital output pin is either HIGH (5 V) or LOW (0 V). A digital input pin reads a switch or sensor as HIGH or LOW. This lesson teaches you to control an LED and read a button.
real_world_application: Every embedded system uses digital I/O: turning on a motor, reading a limit switch, triggering an alarm, or detecting a door sensor. Mastering digital I/O is the foundation of all embedded programming.

core_concepts.definition: General Purpose Input/Output. Pins that can be configured as digital input or output.
Digital logic levels. HIGH is typically 5 V (or 3.3 V), LOW is 0 V.
Configures a pin as INPUT, OUTPUT, or INPUT_PULLUP.
Sets an output pin to HIGH or LOW.
Reads the state of an input pin (HIGH or LOW).
Enables the internal pull-up resistor so a button to ground reads LOW when pressed.

step_by_step_explanation: 1. Identify which pins you will use for output (LED) and input (button).
2. In setup(): call pinMode(ledPin, OUTPUT) and pinMode(buttonPin, INPUT_PULLUP).
3. In loop(): read the button with digitalRead(buttonPin).
4. If the button is pressed (LOW), turn the LED on with digitalWrite(ledPin, HIGH).
5. Otherwise, turn the LED off with digitalWrite(ledPin, LOW).
wiring_instructions: Connect LED anode to pin 13 through a 220 O resistor. Connect LED cathode to GND. Connect one button terminal to pin 2. Connect the other button terminal to GND. The internal pull-up holds pin 2 HIGH; pressing the button pulls it LOW.
diagram_specification: Arduino Uno with LED on pin 13 (through resistor to GND) and button on pin 2 (to GND). Internal pull-up enabled.

code_examples.explanation: The LED mirrors the button state. INPUT_PULLUP means a pressed button reads LOW.

line_by_line_code_explanation: const int led = 13; — defines the LED pin number.
const int button = 2; — defines the button pin number.
pinMode(led, OUTPUT); — configures pin 13 as an output.
pinMode(button, INPUT_PULLUP); — configures pin 2 as input with internal pull-up.
digitalRead(button) == LOW — checks if button is pressed (pulled to ground).

interactive_experiment.description: Toggle a virtual button and observe the LED state change.
interactive_experiment.expected_behavior: LED turns on when button is pressed, off when released.

expected_observations: LED is off when button is not pressed.
LED turns on immediately when button is pressed.
LED turns off immediately when button is released.
common_mistakes: Forgetting pinMode() — pin may not work as expected.
Using INPUT instead of INPUT_PULLUP and forgetting external pull-up resistor.
Connecting button to VCC instead of GND with INPUT_PULLUP (reads always LOW).
Reversing LED polarity (LED does not light).
Using analog pins without understanding their digital capability.
troubleshooting_steps: LED does not light: check polarity, check resistor, check pin number.
Button does not respond: check wiring, check pinMode, check for floating input.
LED always on: button may be wired to VCC instead of GND.
LED always off: check if button reads correctly with Serial Monitor.
safety_notes: Always use a current-limiting resistor with an LED.
Do not connect a motor or high-current device directly to a GPIO pin.
Ensure the Arduino is powered via USB or a regulated supply.

knowledge_check.question: With INPUT_PULLUP, what does a pressed button (to ground) usually read?
knowledge_check.explanation: The pull-up holds the pin HIGH; pressing to ground pulls it LOW.

knowledge_check.question: Which function configures a pin as an output?
knowledge_check.explanation: pinMode(pin, OUTPUT) configures the pin. digitalWrite() sets its value.

mini_challenge: Modify the code so the LED toggles (on/off) each time the button is pressed, instead of mirroring the button state.
extension_activity: Add a second LED and button. Make one LED mirror the button and the other toggle.
assumptions: No debouncing needed for simple demonstration.
intended_learning_outcome: Learner can configure digital pins, read a button, and control an LED in response to input.
